AUTHOR: Naval
TITLE: FishDrop: Estimation of reef fish population density and biomass using stereo cameras
SPECIES: Reef fish; 25-class and 182-class CNN classifiers (species not listed)
DATA: Own diver-deployed stereo GoPro rig videos, >20 sites; test 20 two-minute clips from 20 sites
V_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'The videos were obtained at different depths, times of day, and visibility conditions. An inclusion criterion of at least 10 meter visibility was imposed.'
D_EV: no statement found (Sec. III.E only: 'A collection of these images for each species are set aside for training the CNN classifier.')
R_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'We measure the performance of these algorithms on 20 two-minute clips from fish videos taken from 20 different sampling sites in the Verde Island Passage'
C_EV: Sec. IV.A / Table I: 'The precision and recall values were obtained from 300 randomly selected segmented images.' Precision 0.71; water particles mistaken for fish blobs.
E_EV: Tables I-II report only segmentation 'Precision 0.71 Recall 0.94' and classifier 'Accuracy 96.1 % 91.3 %'; density/biomass/MaxN computed but not reported or evaluated.
ARCH: Motion-based blob segmentation + fine-tuned AlexNet CNN classifier (Caffe) + stereo 3D length/density/biomass
NOTE: V: footage restricted to >=10 m visibility (a stated threshold, not per-clip measurement) -> V_ALL=N per P1; depth and time-of-day mentioned, qualitative observation that performance degrades at ~5 m depth vs >=10 m (surface lensing) coded V6=P. Could alternatively be argued V_ALL=P. C5: segmentation precision from 300 randomly sampled segmented images treated as verification-sample FP rate; no threshold value. Train/test separation of CNN unknown. PLAT: diver-placed stationary stereo rig moved along transect. Pretraining of AlexNet not explicitly stated (only 'fine-tuned').
